title: Flatness and the closed fibre make the tensor-map kernel equal its maximal-ideal multiple
statement: Let $A_0,A,C,B$ be commutative local rings with local maps $\alpha:A_0\to A$, $\gamma:A_0\to C$, $\varphi:A\to B$, $\psi:C\to B$ such that $\psi\gamma=\varphi\alpha$; use $\alpha,\gamma$ as their algebra structures. Suppose $\alpha$ induces an isomorphism of residue fields. Let $D=C\otimes_{A_0}A$ [def-weil-module-base-change] and $F:D\to B$ be a surjective ring map with $F(c\otimes a)=\psi(c)\varphi(a)$. Assume $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\ker(C\xrightarrow{\psi}B\to B/\mathfrak m_A B)=\mathfrak m_0 C$. Put $K=\ker F$ and $L=\mathfrak m_A D$, extended using $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. Then $K\subseteq LK$ as $D$-submodules of $D$. No finite coefficient map, Noetherianity, completeness, or formal smoothness is assumed.

source.place: Remark 07NS part (4) and Proposition 07NQ kernel-tensor paragraph; tensor exactness part of step 7 of lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-over-finite-coefficient-map.

proof.text: The tensor formula makes F A-linear and identifies its restrictions to A and C with φ and ψ. Its surjectivity gives 0→K→D→B→0 exact as A-modules. Since B is flat over A, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] says that K⊗_A k→D⊗_A k is injective, for k=A/m_A. Identify these tensor products with the quotients K/m_A K and D/m_A D.

Surjectivity of the residue map gives A=α(A₀)+m_A. Balancing reduces each pure tensor, and then each sum, modulo m_A D to c⊗1. A class of this form mapping to zero has ψ(c)∈m_A B, hence c∈m₀C by the assumed kernel equality. Write c=Σγ(x_i)c_i with x_i∈m₀; then c⊗1=Σc_i⊗α(x_i)∈m_A D since α is local. Thus D/m_A D→B/m_A B is injective.

The image of K/m_A K in D/m_A D is zero by exactness. Its injectivity therefore gives K/m_A K=0. This says K=m_A K as A-submodules, equivalently K=(m_A D)K as D-submodules. The displayed inclusion follows.
